name: FLOWSTACK Theme system
purpose: Author, compile, and integrate a project theme without changing Brick component meaning or moving application runtime ownership into Theme.
decisionOrder: Identify brand and product colors as project palettes and roles before mapping any value to Brick.
Install a released Brick version whose theme contract revision is supported by Theme.
Map only UI meanings Brick owns into brick.light and brick.dark; keep charts, syntax, editorial, and campaign colors in project roles or namespaced extensions.
Override a complete atomic Brick family or inherit that entire family from Brick defaults.
Compile at build time, review the contrast report and static artifacts, then ship the CSS rather than the compiler.
Let the application own activation, saved preference, fonts, assets, portals, and first-paint behavior.

rules.statement: Keep theme definitions JSON-compatible and deterministic; do not use functions, DOM state, environment-dependent values, or runtime callbacks.
Compile against the theme-contract.json exported by the installed Brick package and do not maintain a copied semantic-token list.
When one member of an atomic Brick color family changes, provide the complete family for that appearance or inherit the complete Brick default.
Map values by semantic UI meaning; never misuse warning, danger, success, or information merely to obtain a desired hue.
Keep unlimited non-Brick brand, visualization, syntax, editorial, and product colors in palettes, roles, or namespaced extensions.
Treat insufficient or unprovable Brick-declared contrast pairs as build failures; do not round a failing ratio into a pass.
Ship compiled static CSS and keep @flowstack-ui/theme in build tooling unless a separately qualified runtime adapter is introduced.
Keep theme selection, persistence, pre-paint setup, font and asset loading, and portal-container coordination in the application.
Do not add theme breakpoints expecting them to recompile Brick media queries; Brick component breakpoints and application layout policy have separate owners.
Use components only for inputs explicitly audited in the Brick contract; keep local component token overrides local.

brick: semantic UI roles and component recipes
atomic families, contrast pairs, and approved component inputs
theme: compatibility, completeness, alias, and contrast validation
deterministic CSS, token, manifest, and report artifacts
application: first paint, portals, routes, and product art direction

validation: Validate the definition envelope before compiling.
Compile against the exact installed Brick contract revision and review every diagnostic.
Confirm theme.report.json contains one passing result for every declared pair and supported appearance.
Verify generated artifacts are byte-stable and committed only when the application owns committed build output.
Build the production application and verify explicit light, dark, nested appearance, portal, first-paint, and forced-colors behavior where applicable.
Confirm the browser bundle does not contain the Theme compiler.
